served.stem: Diethyl pimelate (diethyl heptanedioate, drawn) is subjected to NaOEt and then acidic workup. Predict the major Dieckmann condensation product.

answer.line: The alpha carbon attacks the far ester, closing C2 through C7: a six-membered ring, with the other ester left beside the new ketone.

steps: Find the attacker and the target: the alpha carbon C2, next to one ester, and the C=O carbon C7 of the other ester.
Count the ring they close: C2, C3, C4, C5, C6 and C7, six atoms. C1 stays outside as the ester group.
Ethoxide leaves from C7, which becomes the ring ketone, and the ester on C2 stays: ethyl 2-oxocyclohexane-1-carboxylate.

choices.note: Six-membered ring: pimelate closes six, as adipate closes five.
An open chain like this is what a Claisen between two molecules gives. With both esters on one chain, the chain bites its own tail and a ring closes.
The five-membered ring comes from diethyl adipate, one carbon shorter. Pimelate has seven chain carbons and closes six.
This counts all seven chain carbons into the ring. The ring runs from C2 to C7; C1 stays outside as the ester.
Turning the ketone into an alcohol needs a hydride like NaBH4. Acid workup only protonates the enolate.

student.lockIt: Dieckmann ring size: count from the alpha carbon to the other C=O carbon. Adipate closes five, pimelate six.
